levels.mission: The team is onboarding. Before touching the cluster, prove you can map the four core Kubernetes building blocks to what they actually do.
levels.hint: A Service provides network access, a Deployment manages lifecycle, ConfigMap stores config, Secret stores secrets.
levels.intro: Match each Kubernetes object to its purpose:

pairs.definition: Manages rolling updates and maintains the desired number of pod replicas
Provides a stable network endpoint and load-balances traffic across matching pods
Stores non-sensitive configuration data consumed by pods as env vars or volume files
Stores sensitive data like passwords and tokens in an obfuscated, base64-encoded form

levels.mission: A new engineer is debugging networking and storage issues. They need to identify which object controls which layer of the cluster.
levels.hint: Ingress handles HTTP routing, HPA auto-scales pods, PVC requests storage, Namespace isolates workloads.
levels.intro: Match each networking and storage object to what it controls:

pairs.definition: Divides a cluster into isolated virtual sub-clusters for separate teams or environments
A request for storage that binds to a PersistentVolume provisioned by the cluster
Routes external HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Services based on hostname or URL path rules
Automatically adjusts pod replica count based on CPU, memory, or custom metrics

levels.mission: The SRE team is auditing advanced workload types. Match all five specialised controllers to their operational purpose.

lines: Type       Resource  Default Request  Default Limit

levels.hint: StatefulSet = ordered stable pods, DaemonSet = every node, Job = one-shot task, CronJob = scheduled, LimitRange = default resource caps.
levels.intro: Match each advanced Kubernetes controller to its purpose:

pairs.definition: Manages pods with stable network identity and ordered, persistent storage — ideal for databases
Ensures exactly one pod runs on every node in the cluster — used for log agents and monitors
Runs pods to successful completion for one-off batch tasks such as migrations or report generation
Creates Jobs automatically on a repeating cron schedule — for backups, reports, and cleanup tasks
Enforces default resource request and limit policies for all containers in a namespace
